## Specific task description

Task instruction: Grab the flat-bottomed mouse and set it on the Gray mat.

Task description: Move the dark mouse on the right side of the table to the gray rectangular mat below and to its left. The target is near the center of the mat, and the required orientation and release conditions must also be met.

Success criteria: Place the mouse near the gray mat's center in both horizontal directions, flat with its bottom down and in the specified orientation. Both grippers must be open. Merely placing it somewhere within the mat is insufficient.

## Execution tips

- Approach the mouse from above and span its short dimension to grip straight sidewalls around its middle. Avoid narrowed ends and the rounded top to reduce pushing or slipping during closure.
- Make the gripper opening slightly wider than the selected grasp point. Before closing, confirm the pads are on both sides and the fingertips are not against the table, avoiding a grasp that only presses on top of the mouse.
- If turning it, wait until the mouse is off the table and has enough surrounding clearance. Avoid rotating against the tabletop, which could drag the mouse or sweep into the gray mat.
- Keep the bottom face level during placement and release only after the gray mat supports the mouse securely, reducing shifts from a tilted landing.
- The materials do not specify how the mouse model’s direction maps to its visible front and rear. Use runtime pose feedback to confirm the required orientation rather than judging it only by whether it is parallel to the mat edge.
